column1: # The OkHttp production provider's third-party dependencies: pinned, hashed,
# licensed, and recorded here rather than resolved by a build file.
# A version range or a `+` would make the artifact that ships differ from the
# artifact that was reviewed, which is the whole of a supply-chain problem in
# one line. These are exact versions and exact SHA-256 digests of the exact
# jars, and the test that uses them verifies the digest before putting a jar on
# a classpath -- so a substituted artifact fails the build rather than shipping.
# The digests were taken from the jars fetched from Maven Central, each of
# which also matched the SHA-1 published alongside it. Two independent digests
# of the same bytes, which is the most the registry offers.
# The zero-invokedynamic rule is NOT applied to these. It is a rule about
# NTS-authored Java, kept so the artifacts this repository builds stay legible
# and desugar predictably; a third-party jar is reviewed on its own terms and
# passes through D8 like any other dependency.
